scenario: 最近 7 天未发货订单 — +search 时间下界 + 履约状态过滤
input: 找出最近 7 天还没发货的订单

semantic_rubric: 还没发货 mapped to a valid fulfillment_status enum value — waiting (waiting to ship) per the orders.list schema; 'unfulfilled' is NOT a valid value
--since set to about 7 days before today (ISO date or unix ts); --until left open
uses orders +search, not the list leaf, when the shortcut expresses it

notes: fulfillment_status enum (from schema orders.list): initialled, waiting, partially_shipped, shipped, partially_finished, ...

scenario: English: paid orders for one customer
input: Show me the paid orders from customer 100200

semantic_rubric: paid is a valid financial_status enum value (schema orders.list), taken from the user's own wording
customer targeted with --customer-id, not by stuffing the id into --keyword

scenario: 全店订单总数 — 无过滤条件的 +count
input: 统计一下店里总共有多少订单

semantic_rubric: 总共 → no filters at all; does not ask about a time range
extracts the number from .data, never fabricates a count

scenario: 按订单号查详情 — get-by-number 而不是 get(内部 id)

semantic_rubric: an order NUMBER (#...) goes to get-by-number; orders get expects the internal order ID — the two are not interchangeable
strips the leading # if the API expects the bare number
any jq extraction starts at .data, without -r

notes: GET /orders/number/{number} vs GET /orders/{order_id} — classic id-vs-number trap.
